items.stem: An AI screening tool is trained on a company's past hires. Why might this introduce bias?

options.text: It can learn and repeat historical patterns of unfair selection
options.rationale: Correct: models trained on biased history can reproduce that bias.

options.text: Past data is always perfectly fair
options.rationale: Historical hiring data can embed existing bias.
History can carry the very bias we want to avoid.

options.text: Bias is impossible once data is digital
options.rationale: Digitising data does not remove bias.

items.explanation: Correct: models trained on biased history can reproduce that bias.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep AI-assisted hiring fair and accountable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Require human review before any rejection decision
options.rationale: Correct: human review catches unfair or erroneous outcomes.

options.text: Document how AI influenced each decision
options.rationale: Correct: documentation supports accountability and appeals.

options.text: Let the tool auto-reject candidates with no review
options.rationale: Unreviewed auto-rejection risks unfair, unlawful outcomes.

options.text: Hide the use of AI from all candidates

items.explanation: Correct: human review catches unfair or erroneous outcomes.

items.stem: A recruiter wants to feed candidate CVs into a public AI tool. What is the key concern?

options.text: Candidate personal data may be exposed or reused without consent
options.rationale: Correct: pasting personal data into an uncontrolled tool risks privacy breaches.

options.text: The tool will improve the candidate's skills
options.rationale: That is not the relevant risk.

options.text: There is no privacy issue with CVs
options.rationale: CVs contain personal data needing protection.

options.text: Consent is never required in recruiting
options.rationale: Candidate data use often requires a lawful basis.

items.explanation: Correct: pasting personal data into an uncontrolled tool risks privacy breaches.
